title: MINOR: Tweak ConsumerAssignorBenchmark
body:
For the events other than FULL, ConsumerAssignorBenchmark fed the output
of the assignor back as the current assignment, so the incremental
events measured whatever set types the assignor returned (RangeSet for
the range assignor). The coordinator replays the target assignment from
its records instead, and Assignment.fromRecord builds a HashMap with a
HashSet per topic. The benchmark now builds the current assignment of
every member the same way, for every assignor and every event.

The member, topic and partition counts now form a plain cross product in
which every
combination is a valid group:
- memberCount: 5, 50, 500, 5000
- topicCount: 5, 50, 500, 5000
- partitionCount (total over all topics): 5000, 10000, 20000

SKEWED only had topics with a single partition below about three
partitions per topic, because it doubled the partitions per topic from a
base size which grew with the partition count. The topics of the first
tier, two thirds of the topics, now always have a single partition, and
the other tiers split the other partitions, doubling the partitions per
topic from one tier to the next, with every topic within one partition
of its exact share.

The class Javadoc is updated with the number of combinations (8064), the
example jmh.sh runs and the heap the largest groups need (about 1 GB).

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>
